items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: Shapiro was his name. And so she had me to come and speak to Ed Hall.

ctx.x: May be going a little ahead of you, but this was 1945, when I -- I got out of the Army in 1941 five. I went in in '43. So she said, all right. Ponder me (Inaudible). She said, come down to Cafe Society --that's when it was uptown -- and talk with Ed Hall, clarinetist (Inaudible). So, boy, I was afraid because I never played with nothing but big bands, you know, like Lunceford's. And I used to go down there every night, peek -- find me a crack -- I used to peek through at the drummer and see what he was doing and…

But Mary Lou Williams for some reason couldn't stand (Arthur) Trappier this fellow. Shapiro was his name. And so she had me to come and speak to Ed Hall. Sure enough, I did, and so I got a job there, did all right, did quite well. I'm very proud of myself. Perseverance is a great thing. When you're hungry --

oh, you -- I was with that little girl there, my wife, [Irene] Crawford. I used to go down there every night and peek through that crack, standing on the outside, looking in, cold, wet, rain, anything. I just wanted to see what the drummer was doing. He was cutting a show, fast hands.
